name: Fatigue Striations
desc: A fatigue fracture surface read under the microscope: a crack born at a corner flaw creeps outward in nested clamshell beach marks, one shallow arched shell per load block creased by an arrest line, spacing widening exactly as the growth rate does, ratchet steps radiating from the origin — and everything the crack never reached stays as the matte dimpled crater-field of the final overload, shrinking as a raking electron beam wanders the plate, until the specimen lets go and re-etches onto a fresh one.

energy.doc: relief gain and contrast — max drives the clamshell banding and the secondary-electron edge glare hard

scale.doc: microscope magnification about the x/y anchor — max nearly triples the field, resolving striations that were sub-pixel

speed.doc: how fast the specimen lives out its ~96s fatigue life before rupturing and re-etching to the next

density.doc: striation fineness — how many cycles are written per millimetre of crack growth (they stay above the resolving limit at both extremes)

rough.doc: surface roughness and the coarseness of the overload dimples — subordinate texture, never the subject

hue.doc: tint of the metal under the stereomicroscope (the sem plate stays neutral)

style.doc: aesthetic: forensic greyscale SEM plate with edge glare / warm optical stereomicroscope with shallow depth of field / ironbow false colour / topographic contour abstraction as pure line on cream / sumi ink

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the origin, front distortion, ratchet marks and load-block count
